body:
## Summary
- `from_json` for array-like containers (`std::vector`, `std::deque`, `std::set`, ...): loops over the stored `array_t` and calls `push_back` (SFINAE/`priority_tag`), falling back to `insert(end(), ...)` for containers without `push_back`. This also speeds up `std::array<T,N>` (which uses `at(i)`).
- New `GetArray<...>` benchmarks in `tests/benchmarks`.
- The `at(size_type)` / `at(key)` cold-throw change was removed from this PR; it moved to #5838 together with the single "array index N is out of range" helper.

## Numbers (Apple clang 21, -O2, ns per element, best of 7)
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `get<std::vector<int>>` | 4.6 | 1.0 |
| `get<std::deque<int>>` | 11.96 | 1.32 |
| `get<std::array<int,8>>` | 1.66 | 0.95 |
| `get<std::set<int>>` | 114.7 | 74.7 (noisy, allocation-bound) |

## Breaking changes
No breaking changes. No public API change: only the internal loop of `from_json` for array-like containers changes; results and exception types are identical.

Unit tests `conversions1/2` and `element_access1/2` pass; `make amalgamate` run.

comments.body: Update since the last review (written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann): narrowed the PR to the array-to-container `from_json` speed-up. The `at()` changes (`throw_array_index_out_of_range`, `throw_key_not_found`, `ArrayAt` benchmark) were reverted here and move to #5838. Also removed the incorrect claim in the description that the `get_ref` throws were already out of line. Conversions and element-access tests pass.
